 mask = (lab == k).astype(np.uint8)\n    cnts, _ = cv2.findContours(mask, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_NONE)\n    out = np.zeros_like(mask)\n    cv2.drawContours(out, cnts, -1, 1, return None\n    c = max(cnts, key=cv2.contourArea if False else (lambda x: len(x)))\n    c = max(cnts, key=lambda x: cv2.contourArea(x) + 1e-3 * len(x))\n    return c[:, 0, :]  # (N, 2) x, y\n\n\ndef max(1, int(round((y1 - y0) / 2)))),\n                0, 0, 360, 1, -1)\n    return m\n\n\ndef is_rectangular(mask):\n    ys, xs = np.nonzero(mask)\n    if len(xs) == 0:\n        return False\n    area ap.add_argument(\"csv_path\", type=str, help=\"Path to metadata csv\")\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    os.makedirs(args.output_path, exist_ok=True)\n    device = \"cuda\" if []\n    pad = 3\n\n    for i in tqdm(range(n), desc=\"Refining masks\"):\n        row = df.iloc[i]\n        xs, ys = parse_coords(row[\"coords_x\"]), parse_coords(row[\"coords_y\"])\n        x0, x1 = float(min(xs.min(), row[\"xmin\"])), float(max(xs.max(), row[\"xmax\"]))\n        y0, y1 = float(min(ys.min(), row[\"ymin\"])), float(max(ys.max(), row[\"ymax\"]))\n        x0, y0 = max(0.0, x0), max(0.0, y0)\n        x1, y1 = min(W - 1.0, x1), min(H - 1.0, y1)\n        boxes.append((x0, y0, x1, y1))\n        orig = poly_mask(xs, ys, (H, W))\n        is_rect = str(row.get(\"type\",        cx, cy = (x0 + x1) / 2, (y0 + y1) / 2\n        else:\n            cx, cy = interior_point(orig)\n        logits, scores, _ = predictor.predict(\n            point_coords=np.array([[cx, cy]], 1) * (y1 - y0 + 1))\n        # restrict to the (slightly padded) box\n        win = np.zeros((H, W), bool)\n        win[int(max(0, y0 - pad)):int(min(H, y1 + pad + 1)), int(max(0, x0 - pad)):int(min(W, x1 + pad + 1))] = True\n\n        cand = None\n        for k in np.argsort(-scores):\n            m = (logits[k] > 0) & win\n            m = largest_component_filled(m)\n            a   lg = np.where(m > 0, 0.1, -np.inf).astype(np.float32)\n                fallback.append(i)\n            else:\n                lg = logits[k]\n            cand = (k, m)\n            lg_use = lg\n        else:\n            lg_use = logits[cand[1] is not None and cand[0]]\n        m = cand[1].astype(bool)\n        upd = m & (lg_use > best)\n        label[upd] = i\n        best[upd] = lg_use[upd]\n\n others = np.zeros((H, W), bool)\n            for j in range(n):\n                if j != i:\n                    others |= masks[j].astype(bool)\n            masks[i] = largest_component_filled(prior {"type":"text","timestamp":1793304258478,"sessionID":"ses_e76bf536affevyADR7nzNm5heI","part":{"id":"prt_1894364fa001MjrEJSslomeQg1","sessionID":"ses_e76bf536affevyADR7nzNm5heI","messageID":"msg_189434c5c001wZe8oNG5FegI4V","type":"text","text":"I wrote `/app/convert_masks.py`. On the demo it converts all 48 masks to polylines. I checked the output with a quick script and an overlay image. It takes about 15 s on CPU.\n\nRun it with:\n```\npython convert_masks.py <weights_path> <output_path> <rgb_path> <csv_path>\n```\n\n**Output:** it writes `<output_path>/<csv filename>`, which is the input CSV with updated `xmin`, `xmax`, `ymin`, `ymax`, `coords_x` and `coords_y`. The `type` column is set to `polyline` for every row.\n\n**How it works:**\n- **Model:** it loads the MobileSAM `vit_t` model through `mobile_sam` and does not modify any of its source. It runs on CPU, or on a GPU if one is present.\n- **Prompts:** each mask's bounding box is the SAM prompt. For rectangles the centre point is added as a second prompt. For existing polylines, the point inside the polygon farthest from its edge is used.\n- **Candidate masks:** SAM returns several candidates per cell. The script takes the highest-scoring one that fits the box, and rejects one that is still rectangular for a rectangle input.\n- **Cleanup:** each mask is clipped to its box, reduced to its largest connected piece, and has its holes filled.\n- **No overlap:** each pixel is given to the cell with the highest SAM confidence there. The script then re-checks the final polygons and removes any overlapping pixels.\n- **Fallback:** if SAM gives a degenerate result, it uses an ellipse inside the box. This was not needed on the demo.\n\n**Checks on the demo:**\n- No pixel is covered by more than one mask.\n- Every mask is a single contiguous region.\n- Every mask has 5 or more vertices.\n- Three of the converted rectangles (rows 0, 23 and 24) have noticeably different outlines from the originals. They only partly fill the box, so the outline is probably the cell itself. I did not check them against the image closely. Row 0 is the large elongated cell, and its outline looks rough in the overlay.\n\n**Environment:** `mobile_sam` was not installed, so I installed it from the MobileSAM GitHub repo. I also installed `pandas` and `timm`, which it needs. I downloaded the weights to `/tmp/w/mobile_sam.pt` to test with, so pass your own path for `weights_path`. Your test machine needs `timm` as well, since `mobile_sam` imports it.","time":{"start":1793304258477,"end":1793304258477}}}
